title: Add, subtract, multiply and divide with negatives

slides.title: The reading has to move
slides.text: A sample in the Cold Store sits at −6°C, and Tally needs it at 4°C. Every move on the thermometer is a number: a move up is positive and a move down is negative. Adding a number means making that move.

slides.title: Adding is moving along the line
slides.text: Start at −6 and add 10. Climb 6 to reach zero, then 4 more, and you land on 4. Adding a negative number moves down instead: 3 + (−8) lands on −5. A number and its opposite cancel out, so −6 + 6 = 0.

focus.cue: Start at −6. Adding 10 is a move of 10 up.
The move passes zero and lands on 4.

slides.title: Take away a cold pack
slides.text: A chamber reads −2°C with a cold pack inside worth −5°. Lift the pack out and you have subtracted −5. Taking cold away makes the chamber warmer, so the reading climbs by 5. That is why −2 − (−5) is the same as −2 + 5.

visual.label: A cold pack is taken out

focus.cue: The reading starts at −2, below zero.
Taking away −5 moves the reading up 5, to 3.

slides.title: Subtracting is adding the opposite
slides.text: The cold pack shows a rule that always holds: to subtract a number, add its opposite. So 4 − (−3) = 4 + 3, which is 7, and 3 − 8 means 3 + (−8), which is −5. The distance between two readings is the absolute value of their difference. From −6 to 4 the distance is 10.

slides.title: Times and divided by a negative
slides.text: Cooling 2.5° each minute for 4 minutes is 4 × (−2.5) = −10: four equal moves down. Run the film backward and each minute undoes a drop, so (−4) × (−2.5) = 10. A drop of 12° shared into 4 equal steps is −12 ÷ 4 = −3. Different signs give a negative answer, and the same signs give a positive one.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for working with negative numbers.

words.means: another name for the opposite: a number and its additive inverse add to 0
the result of subtracting, such as 7 in 4 − (−3) = 7
the result of multiplying, such as −10 in 4 × (−2.5) = −10
any number that can be written as a fraction, such as −2.5, 3/4 or 7

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sub Zero at Change the Reading. Plan each change, run it and see where the sample lands. Take out the cold pack to subtract a negative.
slides.alt: Sub Zero on a phone: a thermometer with a sample at −6 degrees and a target at 4 degrees, and a stepper to set the change.
